newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline steady despite deals.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline steady despite deals.

text.p: A Japanese buyer's purchase of two cargoes late Friday helped support prices in a current soft market, traders said.
The same Japanese trader who had purchased three cargoes totalling at least 150,000 barrels of 92-octane gasoline for June lifting on Thursday have bought two more cargoes on Friday.
The trader bought a further 100,000 barrels of 92-octane supplies in two cargoes for June 5-9 and June 8-12 loading at $23.60 and $23.30 respectively on free-on-board Singapore basis.

A spate of offers earlier in the day had placed fears that the market remained long but the purchases have removed some lengths. However, sentiment remains shade soft as supplies are more than adequate to meet demand, traders said.
Asian naphtha prices tipped higher as buying interests start picking up. South Korea and Japanese term buyers have begun to enquire for first half July requirements, traders said.
But traders said the overhang in the prompt market may spill into July.
A Japanese trader said arbitrage window is precariously closed currently and may open easily as the European market is also weak.
India's naphtha offer for May and June would also add pressure to the current market.
Saudi Aramco term naphtha talks reached a deadlock ahead of the weekend with end users unwilling to lower bids to meet Aramco target offer of $15 per tonne premia for its full range naphtha.
Most buyers were willing to accept the $17 per tonne premium offer for the A-180 paraffinic naphtha.
In the naphtha swaps market, both June and July were up by a marginal 5-10 cents at $21.75/$22.00.
